label: is-fix-27-31
topic: Fixes for open issues #27 to #31 of fractastical/delphi
summary:
One of the five issues is resolved, two are partly done and two need a single fact each from Amit; none has any comment on GitHub yet. All files are in D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents4/is-fix-27-31/; nothing was posted and the repo was not touched.

- #27 (binding affinity): I wrote and ran a script on a fresh ChEMBL pull for two targets. Measurement noise is 0.5 to 0.7 pKi, which caps a perfect predictor at r 0.69 to 0.95 depending on how wide the target's affinity range is. The ceiling-versus-leakage verdict combines this with the earlier q2-data and q2-critic records, which I did not re-open. The cycle-consistency angle is untested.
- #28 (Mamou-Mani): needs Amit to confirm whether the meeting meant the London architecture practice. A three-step first-engagement plan is drafted for a yes.
- #29 (Formlabs): the record still shows no published swelling coefficient or water diffusivity for any resin. I drafted a proposed set of ten and a strip-soak measurement protocol. The ten are a proposal, and three were picked for stiffness with no water figure seen.
- #30 (Lean grant): needs Amit's decision. By my reading of the law names, only about 8 of the 14 unproved laws have mathematical content; five look like data records and one is retired. I recommend those 8 plus the three question-2 statements. I did not open each registry entry, and the source of the 3-million-token figure is unknown.
- #31 (.life format): a grep confirms the format has no words for sensing or movement. I drafted a behaviour block, three reader rules and a six-step validation chain. None of it is implemented or tested.

Everything for #28 to #30 rests on earlier agent records in the repo, not on pages I re-fetched today.

findings.claim: #27 Lean for Bio, question 2: why don't binding-affinity prediction models work well?: RESOLVED - wrote and ran a noise-floor script on a fresh ChEMBL pull (CHEMBL203 all 661 Ki rows; CHEMBL244 first 1000 of 4125). Per-measurement noise s = 0.525 pKi over 99 cross-document pairs, or 0.71 over the 54 pairs with non-identical values. Within-target ceiling r_max is 0.845 / 0.689 for EGFR and 0.948 / 0.902 for factor Xa. Between-target share is 0.0 on these two targets (same mean), so the 39-target figure in q2-data.json (7.7 % Ki) stands. Verdict written: noise is a ceiling near r 0.85-0.95 on wide-range sets, leakage explains the drop on clean splits, and the rest is model failure. Cycle-consistency angle not tested; the three Lean statements are not written.

lay_summary: Five open questions on the project's public list needed answers, and I worked on each one.

For the drug question, I checked how much two labs disagree when they measure the same drug on the same protein. They disagree enough that even a perfect computer guess could never match the lab numbers exactly.
Two questions can only be finished by the project lead, because each needs one fact only he knows: which partner was meant, and where a number of 'tokens' came from.
For the 3D-printing plastics, nobody has published how much they grow when wet, so I wrote down a simple soak-and-measure test to find out.
For the organism file format, I checked that it has no way to say 'when light hits here, move there', and I wrote a draft of how to add that.

glossary.binding affinity: How tightly a drug molecule sticks to its protein target.
glossary.Ki / pKi: A lab number for binding strength; pKi is its negative logarithm, so one unit means ten times tighter.
glossary.pChEMBL: ChEMBL's standard negative-log scale for potency numbers such as Ki.
glossary.ChEMBL: A free public database of measured drug-protein activities.
glossary.EGFR, factor Xa: Two well-studied human proteins used here as example drug targets.
glossary.SD (standard deviation): A measure of how spread out a set of numbers is.
glossary.noise floor: The size of the disagreement between repeat measurements of the same thing.
glossary.attenuation ceiling: The best correlation any predictor can reach when the answers it is scored against are themselves noisy.
glossary.Pearson r: A score from -1 to 1 for how well two lists of numbers rise and fall together.
glossary.variance split (between/within target): How much of the spread in the data comes from differences between proteins versus differences among drugs on one protein.
glossary.leakage: When test examples are too similar to training examples, so a model looks better than it is.
glossary.clean split: A way of dividing data so the test set is not similar to the training set.
glossary.cycle consistency: The rule that energy differences added around a closed loop of molecules must sum to zero.
glossary.Lean: A computer program that checks mathematical proofs line by line.
glossary.theorem: A statement proved from stated assumptions.
glossary.pinned law / registry placeholder: A law listed in the project's fixed list that has a name but no checked proof yet.
glossary.hygroscopic expansion coefficient: How much a material grows in length for each percent of water it soaks up.
glossary.water diffusivity: How fast water spreads into a material.
glossary.Fickian uptake: The standard simple model of water soaking in by diffusion.
glossary.ASTM D471: A standard test for how much a rubbery material changes after soaking in a liquid.
glossary.bilayer: Two layers glued together; if one swells and the other does not, the strip bends.
glossary.PLA / PETG: Two common plastics used in 3D printing.
glossary.Fuse powder / Form 4 resin: Formlabs materials for its powder-fusing printers and its liquid-resin printers.
glossary..life / .organism format: The project's file formats for describing a designed organism, where every value says whether it was measured, assumed or unknown.
glossary.kind and scope: The format's required labels on every value: how it is known, and what it does and does not apply to.
glossary.not-established: The format's label for a value that was looked for and does not exist yet.
glossary.sensor / actuator: A part that detects something (here light) and a part that moves in response.
glossary.xenobot: A tiny living machine built from frog cells.
glossary.token: The unit of text an AI model reads or writes; grants may be counted in tokens.
glossary.grep: A tool that searches files for words.
